speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you describe when the rash first appeared and what it looks like?

speaker: Patient
text: 3-month-old boy. The parents report that the rash has been present for several weeks, noting that it sometimes appears red and scaly, especially during cold weather. The patient was born at 36 weeks' gestation and has been generally healthy since. The patient's father has a history of psoriasis.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the rash involve the scalp as well, and have you noticed any similar lesions on his diaper area or flexural surfaces? I also need to know if he seems itchy or irritable, or if the rash improves with gentle moisturizing.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Rash on scalp and forehead. I also have Erythematous patches, Greasy yellow scales, Worse in cold weather.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the greasy yellow scales on the scalp and forehead in a 3-month-old, this presentation is classic for infantile seborrheic dermatitis. DIAGNOSIS READY: Infantile Seborrheic Dermatitis
